title: Diff Evidence Bundles
description: Evidence-bundle diff as a hash-bearing server kernel. From two parsed JSON bundles (bundle_a = baseline, bundle_b = comparison) plus an optional as_of timestamp, the node classifies each side the way the estate's verification desk does (OCG artifact carrying an execution_hash, chain given as a step-artifact array or a steps array, evidence bundle carrying a subject_hash without an execution_hash, or a records array) and reports, values only, what moved: hash- and digest-bearing fields, version-bearing fields, a normalized human-accountability view (approval, rejection and override membership sets plus threshold and gate-policy fields, with legacy records arrays, embedded sign_off members and the converged evidence-bundle shape all normalizing to the same comparison keys so a shape migration alone is never a diff row), and the verdict (verification_result first, then explicit verdict-family fields, then derived from a checks array) with a regressed flag when the verdict moved toward fail, reject or hold. Nesting is capped at 200 levels; unrecognized inputs, missing sides and a missing as_of on an override-bearing pair are refused by throw with a named reason. The node ports the internal comparison math of the existing root page bundle-diff.html, which stays untouched, so an MCP auditor gets an execution_hash-bearing result instead of a page-only view. Built by row BUNDLE-DIFF-KERNEL-1, 2026-10-20.

bundle_a.description: Baseline: a parsed OCG artifact (execution_hash), a chain (steps), an evidence bundle (subject_hash, no execution_hash) or a records array. Required.

bundle_b.description: Comparison bundle, same accepted shapes as bundle_a. Required.

as_of.description: ISO 8601 clock reading for override freshness; required when an override record is present.

mcp_tool_definition.name: compute_diff_evidence_bundles
mcp_tool_definition.description: Evidence-bundle diff: classify two parsed JSON bundles (artifact, chain, evidence bundle or records array) and report values-only what moved: hash fields, versions, normalized accountability sets, verdict with regression flag. as_of supplies the override clock. Unrecognized inputs are refused by throw.

bundle_a.description: Baseline: a parsed OCG artifact (execution_hash), a chain (steps), an evidence bundle (subject_hash, no execution_hash) or a records array. Required.

bundle_b.description: Comparison bundle, same accepted shapes as bundle_a. Required.

as_of.description: ISO 8601 clock reading for override freshness; required when an override record is present.

input_class_a.description: Classification of bundle_a: artifact, chain, evidence_bundle or records.

input_class_b.description: Classification of bundle_b: artifact, chain, evidence_bundle or records.

inputs_differ_in_class.description: True when the two sides classify differently.

hashes.description: Hash- and digest-bearing field diff: counts per side, a closed status enum (absent, unchanged, changed) and rows of path, kind (added, removed, changed), from and to.

versions.description: Version-bearing field diff, same shape as hashes.

human_accountability.description: Normalized accountability diff: shapes per side, subject hashes, membership counts, threshold-field counts, a status and rows over approvals, rejections, overrides and threshold fields. A shape migration alone yields zero rows.

verdict.description: Verdict comparison: values and sources per side, a status (absent, unchanged, changed, regressed) and the regressed flag (B moved toward fail, reject or hold while A did not).

changed_section_count.description: How many of the four sections are changed or regressed.

bundles_identical.description: True when no section reports a change.

input_schema_provenance: Each property is exactly the policy_parameters member the kernel reads; there is no other input surface. bundle_a and bundle_b are required and accept the four recognized input classes; as_of is the only optional property and becomes required whenever either bundle carries an override record (the kernel refuses with a named error otherwise, because the source page reads the wall clock at that point and the kernel must stay pure).
